correctness.rationale: A selected cell set with a occupied rows and b occupied columns has residual graph precisely K_(m-a) square K_(n-b). For both residual factors nonempty, residual degree m+n-a-b-2, so absence of K_(1,ell) is equivalent to a=m or b=n or m+n-a-b<=ell+1. Unique occupied support and row/column inclusion-exclusion give the all-size polynomial. For p<m selected cells, a+b<=2p forces p>=ceil((m+n-ell-1)/2); partial permutation matrices attain the bound unless all m rows must be hit. Equality forces support sizes (t,t) or, at odd L, (t,t-1)/(t-1,t), giving exactly the claimed factorial/binomial optimizer counts including t=m exceptional boundary. Rebuilt rook adjacency and residuals independently, checking the feasibility equivalence for 23 triples with m=2,3 and n<=4. The general argument is structural, not inferred from finite enumeration.
